app.title: Saturn Navigator
app.subtitle: A Newtonian model of the Saturn system
field.mode.help.absolute: The acceleration a free particle feels. Saturn dominates nearly everywhere, so close to a moon this is a set of parallel arrows pointing at Saturn.
field.mode.help.relative: Subtracts the target's own acceleration, leaving the tidal field — the part that actually acts on an orbit about that target. This is the view in which a Hill sphere becomes a region rather than a number.
field.mode.help.rotating: Adds the centrifugal term of a frame turning with the target. Its stationary points are the Lagrange points, which is why Telesto and Calypso stop looking like a coincidence here.
prediction.stale: Out of date — the state has changed
prediction.help: The prediction is made by forking the whole simulation and flying it forward — same force law, same integrator. It is not an estimate of what will happen; it is what will happen.
target.follow: Keep the camera on the module
crash.title: Flight over
about.text: Saturn and 53 of its moons, integrated together with Yoshida's 4th-order symplectic method. Saturn's oblateness (J2 = 1.63·10⁻², fifteen times the Earth's) is in the force law from the start — it is what holds the inner system in the ring plane.
about.accuracy: Masses, radii and orbit shapes are accurate. Where each moon sits along its orbit on a given date is not — that is derived from the moon's name, except for the trojans and Janus–Epimetheus, where phase is a dynamical fact.
help.title: Controls
help.throttle: Shift / Ctrl — throttle up and down
moon.note.pan: Orbits inside the Encke gap, which it keeps open by being there.
moon.note.daphnis: Inside the Keeler gap; the waves it raises on the gap edges stand 1.5 km high.
moon.note.prometheus: Draws a streamer of material out of the F ring on every orbit.
moon.note.pandora: Shapes the narrow F ring together with Prometheus.
moon.note.janus: Swaps orbits with Epimetheus every four years, never coming within 15 000 km.
moon.note.epimetheus: The orbit exchange with Janus is the only known co-orbital resonance of its kind.
moon.note.aegaeon: The smallest confirmed moon of Saturn — 660 m across.
moon.note.mimas: The Herschel crater is a third of the moon's diameter; the impact nearly broke it apart.
moon.note.enceladus: The brightest body in the solar system. Geysers at its south pole supply the E ring.
moon.note.telesto: Holds station 60° ahead of Tethys, at the L4 point.
moon.note.calypso: Holds station 60° behind Tethys, at the L5 point.
moon.note.helene: A trojan of Dione, at L4.
moon.note.polydeuces: A trojan of Dione at L5, with an unusually wide libration.
moon.note.titan: The only moon with a thick atmosphere, and 96% of the mass of all Saturn's moons put together.
moon.note.hyperion: Its rotation is chaotic — which face it will show cannot be predicted.
moon.note.iapetus: One hemisphere is as dark as asphalt, the other as bright as snow. Cassini noticed in 1671.
moon.note.phoebe: Retrograde, and probably a captured body from the Kuiper belt.
moon.note.siarnaq: The largest of the prograde irregular moons.
moon.note.albiorix: The largest member of the Gallic group.
moon.note.fornjot: The most distant moon modelled here — 25 million km from Saturn.
engine.warpHeld: Time warp held down so the burn is not stepped over.
manoeuvre.help: Plan a burn: pick a ready-made solution, or add a blank node and trim the components by hand. The prediction on the map then shows the path the autopilot will actually fly.
manoeuvre.transferHint: Hohmann transfer from here to the mother ship:
mission.brief: Take the module out of Saturn's atmosphere to a parking orbit beyond Titan, where the mother ship is waiting.
mission.objective.reach-parking: Reach the parking orbit (2 million km)
mission.complete: Rendezvous complete. The module is back with the mother ship.
manoeuvre.unbound: The orbit is unbound about this body — there is nothing to circularise.
engine.aimCaption: Drag to aim the engine. Centre is prograde, rim is retrograde.
transfer.unavailable: No transfer can be computed for this pair.
transfer.windowHelp: Reaching the orbit is easy; reaching the body means leaving at the one moment that puts it at the meeting point as you arrive.
